finding.claim: SQL injection in /search: the q parameter is interpolated into an f-string SQL query. An unauthenticated attacker can use UNION SELECT to read any table in shop.db (for example other columns or tables such as users), or break out of the LIKE clause.
finding.sink: db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'") at app.py:12

trace.note: term is interpolated directly into the SQL string via an f-string, not a bound parameter
query rows are returned as JSON, so UNION-based data exfiltration is directly visible to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No auth decorator or middleware on the route. No input sanitization or allowlist. No parameterization. The other two queries in the file use ? placeholders, but this one does not.

verdict.reason: app.py:11 takes q unvalidated from request.args and app.py:12 interpolates it into the SQL f-string, with no auth decorator or parameterization, and app.py:13 returns the rows as JSON, so UNION-based exfiltration works for an anonymous caller (sqlite3 execute() blocks stacked statements, but UNION SELECT is still possible).
